Walking the Talk? Green Politicians and Pollution Patterns
abstract: Exploiting three decades of detailed regional data for Germany, we find that when the Green Party is successful at the polls, local hazardous emissions decline. The level of political representation matters, too. Green politicians’ gaining influence at county level is followed largely by a decline in air pollutants that have an immediate adverse health effect. In contrast, when the Green party joins the state government, only greenhouse gas emissions that affect the welfare of future generations via climate change decline. The primary mechanism to achieve lower emissions appears to be a reduction in output, rather than more efficient energy use.
abstract_zh: 利用德国长达三十年的详细地区数据，我们发现，当绿党在选举中取得成功时，当地的有害排放会下降。政治代表权的水平同样重要。绿党政治人物在县一级获得影响力之后，往往会伴随着对那些会立即产生不利健康影响的空气污染物的减少。相比之下，当绿党加入州政府时，只有通过气候变化影响后代福祉的温室气体排放会下降。实现排放降低的主要机制似乎是产出的减少，而非更高效的能源利用。

Finance and Green Growth
abstract: We study how countries' financial structure affects their transition to low-carbon growth. Using global industry-level data, we document that carbon-intensive industries reduce emissions faster in economies with deeper stock markets. Two channels underpin this stylized fact. First, stock markets reallocate investment towards energy-efficient sectors. Second, in countries with deeper stock markets, carbon-intensive sectors engage in more green innovation, resulting in lower carbon emissions per unit of output. Only one-tenth of these industry-level reductions in domestic emissions are offset by carbon embedded in imports. A firm-level analysis of an exogenous shock to the cost of equity in Belgium confirms our findings.
abstract_zh: 我们研究了各国的金融结构如何影响其向低碳增长的转型。利用全球行业层面的数据，我们发现，在股票市场更深入的经济体中，碳密集型行业减排的速度更快。两个渠道支撑了这一典型事实。第一，股票市场将投资重新配置到能源效率较高的部门。第二，在股票市场更深入的国家，碳密集型部门开展了更多的绿色创新，从而使单位产出的碳排放更低。只有十分之一的行业层面国内减排量被进口中所含的碳所抵消。一项针对比利时股权成本外生冲击的企业层面分析证实了我们的发现。
